global_constraints: Preserve the original accepted NotebookLM narration and its timestamps.
Use the downloaded NotebookLM PDF as the semantic reference before image generation; this file is a draft scene map, not final art approval.
Do not copy source watermarks, logos, invented commands, QR codes, or unrelated visual-example content.
Do not imply guaranteed execution, better price, or profit.
Any quantities and prices are illustrative and must be labeled Illustrative.
Render each aspect independently from the same meaning; do not crop desktop art into a Short.

layouts.desktop: 1920x1080. Keep comparison columns and arrows readable. One thesis per frame.
layouts.shorts: 1080x1920. Stack comparisons vertically; keep critical content within x=80..850, y=180..1430, with x=900..1080 and y=1500..1920 quiet.

scenes.thesis: Trigger, execution price, and completed fill are distinct events.
scenes.relationships: Show three separate labeled states connected in order; mark each transition as conditional rather than automatic.
forbidden: A trigger automatically guarantees a full fill
An execution-price label presented as a guaranteed market price

scenes.thesis: Submitting an order is a request whose outcome depends on market constraints.
scenes.relationships: Route one submitted request through a constraints box into alternative outcomes; outcomes must branch rather than appear as required successive steps.
forbidden: Treating every request as a completed trade
Unfilled shown as necessarily failed software

scenes.thesis: Market orders seek immediate liquidity; limit orders bound acceptable prices. Neither guarantees a complete fill.
visible_text: Price and full fill not guaranteed
scenes.relationships: Compare two clearly separated entry-order panels over the complete 7.2-second narration. Market seeks available liquidity across price levels; limit sets a buy-price ceiling or a sell-price floor. Use symbolic bounds rather than adding illustrative numbers. Desktop uses adjacent panels; native vertical stacks the panels without reducing label size.
forbidden: Guaranteed execution
Guaranteed best price
Assuming infinite liquidity
Buy limit described as minimum price
Sell limit described as maximum price
Every limit order is a maker

scenes.thesis: IOC cancels the unfilled remainder; FOK executes the entire quantity immediately or cancels.
scenes.relationships: Compare IOC and FOK using the same available liquidity. If using order quantity 5 and available quantity 2, IOC fills 2 and cancels 3, while FOK cancels the entire 5 without a partial fill. Include Illustrative if numbers appear.
forbidden: IOC requires a complete immediate fill
FOK allows a partial fill
A claim that all venues offer every time-in-force option

scenes.thesis: A stop condition activates an order; the trigger itself is not an execution guarantee.
scenes.relationships: Show condition reached, then a new order submitted; keep a visible separation between trigger and execution outcome.
forbidden: A trigger marker labeled as executed trade
A guarantee of an exit at the stop price

scenes.thesis: Stop-market submits a market order; stop-limit submits a limit order, and neither guarantees a completed exit.
visible_text: Liquidity and venue limits can prevent a full fill
Can remain unfilled after a price gap
scenes.relationships: Use the same price-gap event for both branches. Distinguish the trigger threshold from the submitted limit and from actual fills. The warning must remain legible in both aspect ratios.
forbidden: Stop-market always gets you filled
Stop-limit automatically fills after a gap
Identical icons implying identical execution behavior

scenes.thesis: TWAP and VWAP guide pacing or benchmarks without guaranteeing a better price.
scenes.relationships: Show an order split over time for TWAP and a volume-related execution pattern for VWAP. Present both as execution methods rather than price predictions.
forbidden: Guaranteed lower cost
Guaranteed alpha
VWAP represented as equal slices regardless of volume

scenes.thesis: Linked order conditions can be exchange-hosted or managed by a local strategy.
visible_text: Local conditions depend on the strategy process
scenes.relationships: Show two clearly labeled locations for the condition logic. Local process/connectivity dependence applies to locally managed conditions, not universally to native OCO.
forbidden: All OCO orders are synthetic
Stopping a bot automatically cancels exchange-accepted orders
Universal venue support

scenes.thesis: Specify both desired behavior and failure handling for every order.
scenes.relationships: Present six distinct checklist rows with equal visual weight; keep the final two items visible in the native vertical safe zone.
forbidden: A trading signal presented as the entire execution checklist
Unreadable six-column vertical layout

scenes.thesis: Design the execution system for failures as well as the ideal trade.
scenes.relationships: Reconnect request, constraints, and observed outcome. Keep the final narrated frame through the audio tail; the silent contacts card follows it.
forbidden: A guaranteed winning strategy
A claim that these order choices alone create profit
Ending the frame before the complete final sentence

revision_note: Independent package review combined the two short entry-order scenes into one 7.2-second comparison. All narration segments and source audio remain unchanged; the PDF is a semantic reference, not a mandatory frame count.
